# Golden Rules for Agentic Engineering

Author: Indrajeet Patil
Format: Quarto RevealJS presentation
Canonical URL: https://www.indrapatil.com/agentic-engineering-golden-rules/
Source: https://github.com/IndrajeetPatil/agentic-engineering-golden-rules/
License: CC0 1.0 Universal
Publication date: 2026-10-08
Language: English

## Summary

This slide deck presents golden rules for agentic engineering: using coding agents to boost productivity without compromising quality. Its central claim is that code generation is the easy part. Quality comes from the engineering system around the agent: a codebase that is easy to navigate, a deterministic harness that gives fast feedback, tightly scoped tasks, clean context, and a team culture that keeps humans responsible for what ships.

The talk is aimed at software engineers who ship production software and have at least some experience with coding agents such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI.

## The golden rules

1. DevEx = AgentEx. If humans hunt for context, agents burn tokens too. Clear structure, one-command workflows (such as make setup and make qa), deterministic QA, living documentation (including a short AGENTS.md), and modular design help humans and agents alike.
2. Guardrails. Fast feedback beats orchestration. Use a deterministic harness (formatters, linters, type checkers, tests with coverage gates, Git hooks, secret, dependency, and infrastructure scans, and accessibility audits) to keep the agent's non-determinism in check. Invest in one reliable command that says whether the work is acceptable, run the same gates in CI, and never lower a threshold or disable a check to get green.
3. The Bitter Lesson. Strong models need intent (what you want), not ceremony (how to achieve it). Do not get in the model's way: state the outcome, constraints, acceptance criteria, and what must not change, then give the agent strong tools. Agents must verify their own work: run relevant checks, inspect results, fix failures, and re-check.
4. Scope control. In brownfield projects, introduce changes in reviewable, reversible chunks. Review capacity, not generation speed, is the bottleneck. Capture broader issues as follow-up tasks.
5. Session hygiene. Fresh context beats haunted context. Long sessions accumulate stale assumptions and conflicting instructions. Run one task per session, use one Git worktree per parallel task, and keep durable conventions, decisions, and lessons in the repository (for example, AGENTS.md) rather than in chat history. Reset with a compact handoff: goal, constraints, relevant files, and acceptance checks.
6. Know thy tools. Sometimes the unlock is a hidden tool affordance. Example affordances that users miss include Claude Code voice dictation, Codex built-in image generation, and GitHub Copilot CLI computer use. Read the changelog; these examples are not exhaustive. Official docs were checked on 8 October 2026. When results are poor, check whether the agent had the right context, tools, and feedback.
7. Meta-automation. Automate repeated agent choreography with prompts, skills, slash commands, and workflows. Examples include a dependency-update prompt, a PR screenshot skill, an illustrative review-command shortcut, and a vulnerability-management workflow that triages findings, verifies warranted fixes, and records reasons for rejected findings. Automate coordination; keep judgement human, and run unattended agents only in isolated sandboxes with scoped credentials.
8. Be curious. Be humble. Be kind. AI is not an excuse to become incompetent or disagreeable. AI does not remove responsibility for design, code, tests, security, or communication.
